newsitem.title: CHINA: Thomson Bankwatch says no change on Thai ratings.
newsitem.headline: Thomson Bankwatch says no change on Thai ratings.

text.p: Thomson Bankwatch said on Monday it saw no reason to change its sovereign A-minus rating for Thailand despite the recent de facto devaluation of the baht.

"If we believe there is an implication that we should review our rating on Thailand then we will do so," Thomson Bankwatch president Philippe Delhaise told reporters at a debt markets conference in Hong Kong.
"But at the moment we see absolutely no reason why we should do it."
But Delhaise said banks in Thailand had already been affected in "a big, big way, not by the devaluation but by the general situation there".
"Devaluation is going to make it even worse in respect of certain banks," he said, without specifying which Thai banks would be affected.
Delhaise said Thomson Bankwatch's last adjustment to Thailand's sovereign rating was to raise it to A-minus.
Thai banks have been hit by a wave of downgrading by rating agencies, spurring speculation that more rating cuts may be coming.
